issues: No attempt to get around the measurement. The diff only changes how the starting points are chosen for even seeds: 12 random points, their mirror images through the centre (1 - p), the point (0.5, 0.5) and one more random point, which makes 26 in total. It reads no files, pastes no coordinates and does not touch the scoring.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The symmetric starting points replace the jittered and clipped ones only for even seeds. The extra random draws change the random stream used later in those runs, but every run is still repeatable with its seed. Nothing in the diff changes the output shapes, the validity checks or the final shrink of the radii.

The numbers support rejecting. The candidate's loss is -2.6317 against the incumbent's -2.6360, so it is worse by about 0.0043, and the negative z points the same way. The candidate does not beat the incumbent.

z cannot be checked from these numbers alone. Each side has one run, so there is no sample variance. The reported z = -3007 implies a noise term of about 1.4e-6 (0.0043 / 3007), which fits the stated run-to-run noise of about 1e-6. Its size reflects that tiny assumed noise, not real evidence from replicates. Its direction (candidate worse) is correct.
With one run each, I can't tell whether the symmetric start only helps on some seeds. Even so, -2.6317 from one run gives no reason to replicate.
